learning: If line loss stays at 1.0 per run with progress at or above baseline, sensing resolution is not the limit and the next step is per-track telemetry on where the single loss occurs. If line loss rises or the signal drops to zero mid-tape, the 12 mm footprint is the better choice and the next test is a forward offset change (y 0.06 m) at 12 mm.
notes: Complete runnable package: the iteration 7 baseline with only sensor_size changed from 0.012 to 0.008 m on the same five positions. The controller is held fixed so the race isolates the footprint. All values are inside the contract limits.
rationale: The Builder's intent isolates one change against the iteration 7 baseline: sensor_size 0.012 to 0.008 m on the same five sensor positions (x -0.02 to +0.02 m, y 0.05 m). Iterations 0 to 7 have shown that span, forward offset, mass, wheel radius and wheel track each leave line loss at about 1.0 per run, and steering oscillation has stayed at 0.07 to 0.14, so the robot is not jittering. Sensing has not yet been tested with a footprint smaller than 12 mm on this layout. A smaller footprint gives a sharper per-sensor reading, so the signal changes from covered to partly covered sooner as the line moves. The controller is kept identical to iteration 7 (kp 3.0, ki 0, kd 0.2, base_speed 1.6, weights [-1, -0.5, 0, 0.5, 1], line_loss last_direction) so any change is attributable to the footprint. Sensor weights are unchanged because the positions are unchanged. Risk: with 2 mm gaps between 8 mm footprints at 10 mm spacing, a line centred between two sensors may read low and raise line loss. The signal is normalised by the sum of readings, so a low sum is the main concern; the line-loss threshold is 0.05 on that sum. Expected, not measured: line_loss_events at or below 1.0 per run on the s-bend and oval, slalom below 2.0, and progress at or above the iteration 7 baseline (oval about 0.138, s-bend about 0.148).
